D010-D005_h001.question:
"It's been a rough few months, doctor. About two months ago, I just… snapped. Everything at the bank felt like a personal attack; every time a colleague spoke, I was sure they were talking about me, plotting something. I’d get so angry over the smallest things, yelling at my wife, pacing the house for hours, unable to sit still. My mind was racing, and I’d be talking so fast, my wife would just stare at me, unable to get a word in. I felt like I had to DO something, constantly. I ended up blowing a significant chunk of our savings on investments and gadgets we didn't need – just felt right at the time. To top it all off, I kept feeling like bugs were crawling under my skin, which just fueled my agitation. These sensations, and the feeling that everyone was out to get me, only happened when I was in that extremely high-energy, irritable state.

Then, about five months ago, everything just… shut down. I felt absolutely nothing – no joy, no sadness, just a completely hollow, numb feeling. I couldn’t even decide what to have for dinner, let alone make any significant decisions at work. I lost all interest in everything I used to enjoy. It’s significantly impacted my ability to do my job and even connect with my family. This numbness has been just as debilitating as the manic period."
D010-D005_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h001.answer: D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h002.question: "Doctor, I'm just… exhausted. For the past two months, it felt like I was running on rocket fuel. And I kept hearing voices, whispering about my genius, urging me on. But then, it all crashed. For the last five months, I've been dragging myself through each day.
